title: AI cardiac arrest prediction software linked to fewer ward arrests in Korean hospitals
summary: In a retrospective analysis of a staggered multicenter implementation (164,761 admissions, three secondary hospitals), deployment of DeepCARS, which uses four routine vital signs to predict ward cardiac arrest within 24 h, was associated with a 21% lower ward in-hospital cardiac arrest rate (aRR 0.79, 95% CI 0.65-0.96) and 15% lower in-hospital mortality (aRR 0.85). The design is non-randomized, so confounding is possible.
ai_technology: DeepCARS AI software predicting ward in-hospital cardiac arrest from four routine vital signs

evidence.tested: Retrospective comparison of outcomes across a staggered rollout in three hospitals.
evidence.unknown: Causality and model internals are not established in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Scored ward patients' risk of cardiac arrest within 24 h.
